THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This is an appeal filed by the respondent-Insurance Company aggrieved by the award passed in MVC No.44/2012 dated 06.07.2012.
The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident.

2. It is the case of the claimant that on 13.06.2006 at about 6.00 a.m, when he was riding his TVS motorcycle along with his friend near 12th Cross on B.M.Road, Channapattana, a lorry being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came in opposite direction and dashed against his vehicle.
Due to the said NC: 2023:KHC:37437 impact, he had sustained grievous injuries and he had taken treatment.

3. It is the case of the Insurance Company that the driver of the vehicle was not having a valid driving license to drive a heavy goods vehicle, whereas he was having a license to drive the light motor vehicle.
As it is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

The Court below considering Section 221 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
the light motor vehicle does not exceed 7,500 kilo grams and further on perusal of the permit issued by the RTO in respect of the vehicle which had caused the accident shows that the unloaded vehicle is 5320 kilo grams, which implies that the vehicle which had caused the accident was a light motor vehicle and the driver was having the license to drive the vehicle at the time of the accident.
It is held that both the insurer and the owner of the vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the Court below had committed an error as the driver of the offending vehicle was only having a driving license to drive the light motor vehicle whereas the offending vehicle is a heavy motor vehicle and the Court below ought not to have held that both the owner and the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

He submits that it is clear violation of the terms and conditions of the policy that the driver was not having a valid driving license as he was driving the vehicle and the Insurance Oriental Insuracne Co Ltd vs Ali Asgar on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7522214/

5. Learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that in respect of the very same accident,
when the appeal was filed before this Court in MFA No.10206/2012, this Court had partly allowed the appeal by applying the principles of pay and recover.
He submits that in this case also the same thing will apply.
The Court below without any basis has held that by having a light motor vehicle license he can also drive the heavy transport vehicle.

The Court considered the weight of the vehicle to come to such conclusion that the claimant is the third party to the Insurance policy and if there is any violation of the terms and conditions of the policy, still the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same by the owner of the vehicle.

In view of the above discussions as the driver was having light motor vehicle license and he was driving a goods vehicle, in view of the violation of the terms and conditions of the policy, the Insurance Company shall pay the amount and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
7. It is submitted that the appeal in MFA No.10206/2012 was initially dismissed.
Thereafter they filed RP No.188/2021 dated 15.07.2022, in that review petition, the Court ordered pay and recover.
Accordingly, the appeal of the Insurance Company is partly allowed.
i) The Insurance Company shall pay the compensation amount and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
ii) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
iii) The amount in deposit shall be transferred to the Court below forthwith.
iv) No costs.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
